messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.io>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.io>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.io>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.io>, Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: 
Bcc: 
Date: 2028-06-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: June ops pulse — KPI pre-read and leadership sync

Team — attaching the month-end KPI extract for June (platform level) ahead of next week’s leadership sync. Goal: surface any high-signal deltas so execs can focus questions during the QBR slot.

Quick read:
- Latency: p99 increased by 18% week-over-week in the EU region; correlated with a model rollout on 5/29.
- Cost: total token billing is up 12% month-on-month; embedding calls are the primary driver for the last 10 days.
- Uptime: 99.95% for the month; two brief incidents (12m, 22m) due to autoscaler config during a spike.
- Usage: daily active API clients +9% MoM; top 3 customers account for 42% of peak RPS.

Attachments: platform-kpi-june-2028.xlsx (tabbed: summary, latency-drill, cost-breakdown, usage-rollup) and a one-pager QBR snapshot (QBR-snapshot-reads.pdf).

Asks before Tue leadership sync:
1) Markus — please confirm whether the 5/29 rollout used the new batching shim or the fallback path (I saw differing infra traces).
2) Soojin — any notes from the SRE postmortem for the two incidents? Please add short bullets.
3) Marissa — can you validate whether the embedding surge is from the new similarity product or a sync gone noisy from Acme (Alyssa is on thread).
4) Jonas — highlight any customer-facing follow-ups we should surface to sales.

If you can drop updates inline by EOD Monday I’ll fold them into the pre-read for execs.

Thanks —
Irene
Irene Choi
Director, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: platform-kpi-june-2028.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
[Attachment: QBR-snapshot-reads.pdf (pdf)]

Irene — quick answers inline.

On 2028-06-01 09:12, Irene Choi wrote:
> - Latency: p99 increased by 18% week-over-week in the EU region; correlated with a model rollout on 5/29.

Confirming: the 5/29 rollout used the fallback execution path for the quantized kernels because the optimized kernel build failed a perf regression check in CI. That fallback increases tail latency at sequence lengths >1024. Root cause ticket: INF-5421.

> 1) Markus — please confirm whether the 5/29 rollout used the new batching shim or the fallback path (I saw differing infra traces).

Action: I’ve flagged the kernel build team to re-run the optimized build against the 5/29 model variant with instrumented traces. ETA for a follow-up: Tue COB.

Also: I added a small table to the spreadsheet (latency-drill tab) showing p50/p95/p99 by region and by model family. Please check the numbers; I pulled them from real-time traces and sampling may slightly differ from the daily aggregate.

-Markus
Markus Klein
VP, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Thanks Irene — SRE notes below.

On Fri, Jun 1, 2028 at 11:20 AM Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.io> wrote:
> Action: I’ve flagged the kernel build team to re-run the optimized build against the 5/29 model variant with instrumented traces. ETA for a follow-up: Tue COB.

Incident summary (short):
- Incident INC-8702 (2028-05-31 02:41 UTC): autoscaler double-scaled a transient traffic surge due to a mis-evaluated load metric. Impact: 12 minutes increased error rate for the EU shard. Mitigation: adjusted threshold, rolled back a faulty threshold change in canary.
- Incident INC-8707 (2028-06-02 05:05 UTC): warmup race on dedicated pools after a bulk model swap; impact ~22 minutes. Mitigation: added a short cooldown and increased readiness probe timeout.

Follow-ups I’ll add to the doc:
- Short-term: tighten autoscaler noise floor and add a circuit to prevent double-scale on sub-60s spikes.
- Mid-term: autoscaler rewrite sprint (Q3) to add hysteresis and rate limiting.

I’ll paste a 3-line summary into the QBR-snapshot-reads.pdf for execs.

—Soogin (typo in signature removed)
Soojin Lee
Head of SRE
Redwood Inference

Adding commercial context.

On Sat, Jun 1, 2028 at 03:03 PM Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.io> wrote:
> I’ll paste a 3-line summary into the QBR-snapshot-reads.pdf for execs.

Marissa notes: embedding surge appears to be two-fold: a scheduled similarity-index rebuild for Customer: Acme Analytics (Alyssa — that was OEM-scheduled on 5/28 per our intake logs) and increased ad-hoc similarity calls from a new partner integration that launched 5/25 (unnamed partner; ticket PR-133).

I attached a short CSV extract (top-10 API keys by embedding RPS) in the spreadsheet and flagged rows where customer ownership is ambiguous. Suggested commercial action: 1) For the top ambiguous keys, notify the responsible AE and ask for confirmation inside 48 hours; 2) propose an embedding quota/limit trial for noisy partners to prevent cost overrun while we stabilize the kernel path.

Also attaching a short slide (in the QBR PDF) showing the cost impact projection under three stabilization scenarios (conservative, base, optimistic).

Marissa Cole
Senior Director, GTM Strategy
Redwood Inference
[Attachment referenced: cost-projection-scenarios in QBR-snapshot-reads.pdf]

- Soojin: paste the 2-line incident summary into the QBR PDF and add the short-term autoscaler tweak. ETA: 2028-06-04 EOD.
